note: Type -> requirements and checks. Each check names a verdict tier (letter = exact form, intent = equivalent outcome) and points at the prose section that owns the rationale. The audit (AUDIT.md) runs the checks for a repo's applicable types plus the cross-cutting dimensions; an absent construct is N/A, not a defect.

checks.assert: .editorconfig carries the shared [*.cs] plus ReSharper rule block.
Analyzer severities are enforced; warnings are not relaxed or suppressed wholesale.
NuGet publish uses OIDC Trusted Publishing (NuGet/login), not a stored API key.
The push uses --skip-duplicate and is gated on push, not on an existence check.
PyPI publish uses OIDC Trusted Publishing (no stored token).
The publish job declares environment: pypi and id-token: write, with skip-existing: true.
A ruff configuration is present.
pyright is configured and runs strict on first-party code (src or the integration package) - the strong typing baseline; third-party strictness is relaxed only where a dependency has no usable types.

ruff and pyright config live in pyproject.toml (canonical); standalone .ruff.toml / pyrightconfig.json is a drift finding. A Home Assistant integration is the exception - it follows home-assistant/core standalone-config conventions and is scored by ha.python.conventions instead.
mypy is permitted as an additional type checker (not banned); required for a Home Assistant integration (platinum strict-typing). When used it runs in CI and the editor.
The smoke runtime matrix is a strict non-empty subset of the full matrix.
Per-runtime outputs are aggregated by pattern+merge-multiple into one release-asset-<branch>-<target>, gated !smoke.
Layer cache targets a registry tag (buildcache-<branch>), never type=gha.
Where the Docker Hub overview differs from the project README, a Docker/README.md is published via the docker-readme task (Hub description is size-limited).
The image always re-pushes on publish (base-image refresh), independent of the release-create skip.
Distribution is a GitHub release for HACS (push consumer model); no registry publish.
Follows home-assistant/core Python conventions (pip + requirements*.txt, custom_components/<domain> layout, standalone .ruff.toml + pyrightconfig.json) - expected, not drift.
mypy --strict runs in CI (platinum strict-typing quality-scale tier).
Distribution is a GitHub release data zip pulled into a local EDA install (pull consumer); no package or image registry.
CI runs EDA-specific validation (e.g. kicad-cli ERC/DRC or library linting) - the design-data analogue of the code linters.
Any build-time artifact generation (gerbers, drill, BOM) and version injection is deterministic from the design inputs; aspirational for data-only repos not yet building artifacts.
Codegen output is deterministic from its inputs (no per-run timestamps/GUIDs); runs as a matrix over both branches.
The build reads the committed name->version state file for the tag instead of SemVer2.
The tracker's bump-branch-prefix and branches match the merge-bot's head/base pairs.
The caller passes expect_release_assets:false; the release is tag + source zip + README + LICENSE.
version.json and the NBGV get-version step are retained (they own the tag).
CI runs linting only (markdownlint, cspell, JSON schema, actionlint); no build/test.

workflow.method: Run the WORKFLOW.md 5A static audit and 5B trace scenarios for each applicable D-guarantee against the repo's own Actions.
workflow.note: GitHub Actions may be repo-specific; assert they implement the contract by outcome, not that they match the catalog snippets byte for byte.

checks.assert: main and develop both exist and are protected.
The live develop ruleset matches repo-config/develop.json (normalized diff).
The live main ruleset matches repo-config/main.json (normalized diff).
Every requiredSecret for the repo's publish mechanisms is configured (per spec/secrets.json).
No forbidden secret is present (e.g. a static NUGET_API_KEY on an OIDC repo).
One .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc drives the VS Code extension, the CLI, and CI, and CI runs it.
A cspell.json (not only a workspace word list) drives the extension, the CLI, and CI.
ruff/pyright (Python) and editorconfig/csharpier (C#) configs are shared by editor, CLI, and CI where those languages are present.
Comments are concise, only the non-obvious, no prose narration, and do not grow on re-edit.
ASCII only in agent-authored text: no em-dash (use a spaced hyphen), no smart quotes, no stray non-ASCII.
US English spelling; the shared cspell.json sets language en-US (a bare en accepts British spellings too).

Line endings follow .editorconfig, which carries a global [*] end_of_line = crlf default plus LF pins for execution-sensitive files (shell, Dockerfiles, shebang-executable .py by path); a per-extension-only form lacking the global [*] default is a drift finding. Edits preserve the file's endings.
The README follows the sections and order in spec/readme-structure.md (applicable sections only).
